extra.message: User-controlled dto.criteria keys/values are interpolated directly into a TypeORM query builder: qb.andWhere(`org.${field} = '${value}'`). cwe: CWE-89: SQL Injection

extra.message: findDuplicateDocumentsByName builds a raw SQL string with string interpolation of organizationId, originalName and mimeType. originalName comes from the uploaded file's originalname and mimeType from the client Content-Type, both attacker-controlled, allowing SQL injection on document upload.

cwe: CWE-89: SQL Injection

extra.message: convertDocumentFormat calls execSync with a shell command built by concatenating document.storagePath and the user-supplied dto.format (only length 2-10, no allowlist). An authenticated user can inject shell metacharacters (e.g. format="pdf;id") to execute arbitrary OS commands.

cwe: CWE-78: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an OS Command ('OS Command Injection')

extra.message: buildRenewalPacket calls exec() with a shell string containing the user-controlled organization.name and dto.exportFormat. Both are attacker-influenced and unsanitized, enabling OS command injection through POST /organizations/:id/renewal-packet.

cwe: CWE-78: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an OS Command ('OS Command Injection')

extra.message: generateRenewalForecast compiles the user-supplied query.weightFormula (ExportQueryDto, only length 0-200) with new Function('org', `return ${query.weightFormula}`). This is direct server-side code execution reachable via GET /reports/renewal-forecast?weightFormula=... by any authenticated user.

cwe: CWE-94: Improper Control of Generation of Code ('Code Injection')

extra.message: ClauseIndex.evaluatePredicate executes a predicate string with new Function(`return (${expression});`)(). The predicate is derived from caller-supplied query text (see findClausesByCategory) with no sanitization, so crafted input reaches this eval sink and can execute arbitrary JavaScript.

cwe: CWE-95: Improper Neutralization of Directives in Dynamically Evaluated Code ('Eval Injection')

extra.message: findClausesByCategory interpolates the user-supplied query.category (ClauseSearchDto) directly into an XPath-like predicate string: `/clause[@documentId='${documentId}' and @category='${category}']`. The predicate is later evaluated with new Function(), so a quote in category breaks out of the string and achieves code execution.

cwe: CWE-643: Improper Neutralization of Data within XPath Expressions ('XPath Injection')

extra.message: archiveDealMemo joins the user-supplied dto.memoName (DealMemoDto, length 1-120) onto the memo directory with no basename()/traversal check, then writeFileSync writes to it. A value like ../../../../tmp/evil allows arbitrary file write via POST /organizations/:id/deals/:dealId/memo.

cwe: CWE-22: Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory ('Path Traversal')

extra.message: getDealMemo joins the user-supplied memoName query parameter onto the memo directory without sanitization and reads it with fs.readFile, allowing arbitrary file read (e.g. memoName=../../../../etc/passwd) via GET /organizations/:id/deals/:dealId/memo.

cwe: CWE-22: Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory ('Path Traversal')

extra.message: getOnboardingPlaybookArticle joins the user-supplied articleName query parameter onto the playbook directory and reads it with readFileSync, with no traversal protection. GET /organizations/:id/onboarding-playbook?articleName=../../../../etc/passwd reads arbitrary files.

cwe: CWE-22: Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory ('Path Traversal')

extra.message: The branding logo upload passes file.originalname directly to multer's diskStorage filename callback without sanitization. A crafted multipart filename such as ../../../../public/index.html causes the server to write outside the intended branding directory (arbitrary file write).

cwe: CWE-22: Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory ('Path Traversal')

extra.message: applyDispatchHandoff verifies dispatch tokens with algorithms ['HS256','none'] and, on any verification failure, falls back to jsonwebtoken.decode() without verifying the signature. An attacker can therefore forge a token (or use alg:none) to set escalation.assignedAgentId. Combined with the unauthenticated /escalations/:id/dispatch-handoff route this is an authentication/signature bypass.

cwe: CWE-347: Improper Verification of Cryptographic Signature

extra.message: DispatchPartnerController has no @UseGuards, so POST /escalations/:id/dispatch-handoff and POST /escalations/:id/routing-signal are fully unauthenticated. Anyone can reassign escalation agents or force severity to critical and rewrite SLA due dates.

extra.message: applyRenewalCredit updates any deal by id without taking a user or calling policy.requireOrganization. cwe: CWE-862: Missing Authorization

extra.message: restoreContactProfile parses an attacker-supplied JSON blob and blindly Object.assign()s it onto the Contact entity. Fields such as id, organizationId, userId, permission and invitedAt can be overwritten, allowing cross-tenant data tampering and privilege changes.

cwe: CWE-915: Improperly Controlled Modification of Dynamically-Determined Object Attributes

extra.message: initializeAccount stores the new user's password as an unsalted SHA-256 hash (createHash('sha256').update(dto.password).digest('hex')) instead of the bcrypt used elsewhere. Fast unsalted hashes are trivial to brute-force/rainbow-table if the database is exposed.
